title: Accessibility batch 1: reason-field errors, focus-restore guard, contrast, focus-visible, Escape dismissal, aria-expanded

approvals.evidence: auto-approved: no protected path (components/*.tsx, app/globals.css only), no migration

body.design_ref: None -- no open design question; every fix mirrors an existing pattern already working elsewhere in the codebase (the danger-colour convention, the .chat-input focus-visible pattern, the More button's aria-expanded).

steps.title: useOverlay.ts: guard the focus-restore cleanup on document.activeElement being document.body, so a caller's own explicit focus target is never overwritten.
QuickEditPopover.tsx and StatusCellEditor.tsx: add reasonAttempted state, aria-invalid, aria-describedby and a role=alert error/hint span for the required reason field.
app/globals.css: recompute --text-faint (light and dark) and --h-atrisk/--sev-medium (light) to clear 4.5:1; add .rte:focus-within; add .field-hint/.field-error classes for step 2.
FilterBar.tsx: extract useDismissOnOutsideOrEscape, apply to Columns/More/Legend; add aria-expanded to Columns and Legend.

commit_boundaries: All four steps as one commit: they close seven findings from the same review dimension across four files with no ordering dependency between them, and splitting them would not make any of them independently revertable in a way that matters -- each fix stands alone.
body.rollback: Revert the single commit. Step 1 (useOverlay.ts) carries the only behavioural risk (focus restoration for every overlay in the app); it was verified against every caller (grep confirmed none toggles active=false while leaving its focused DOM node attached) and empirically, in a live browser, by the independent review.
